quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about what the speaker lost, and whether anyone warned them.
quests.explanation: The speaker's effort was wasted because of someone else's carelessness, with no warning. That points to anger.
quests.textToSpeak: They cancelled my appointment again without telling me. I drove forty minutes for nothing.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Compare what normally happens with what is happening now.
quests.explanation: A break in a dependable habit makes the speaker fear something is wrong. This is worry.
quests.textToSpeak: My dad's not picking up. He always answers by the second ring, and that's six calls now.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice the small extra thing the baker did.
quests.explanation: A personal gesture over something the speaker wanted makes them feel warm and pleased. This is happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: The bakery saved the last chocolate cake for me. She even wrote my name on the box.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the 'what if' questions and what they have in common.
quests.explanation: Imagining several ways the meeting could go wrong shows nervousness about tomorrow.
quests.textToSpeak: Tomorrow my parents meet my boyfriend for the first time. What if they don't like him? What if he says something silly?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Compare the amount of effort with the outcome, and listen to the flat ending.
quests.explanation: The result didn't match the effort, and the speaker accepts it quietly without blaming anyone. That's disappointment.
quests.textToSpeak: I practiced for weeks, and I didn't even make the team. Well. That's that.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker didn't know until now.
quests.explanation: The improvement is news to the speaker, and the quick questions show surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: Your grades went up in every subject? Since when? You never told me you were studying that hard.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what the speaker says they've been doing for the past week.
quests.explanation: The week of tension ends with good news, so the speaker can finally relax. Relief is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: The tests came back clear. Everything's normal. I've been holding my breath for a week.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Focus on how the speaker stresses the size of the audience.
quests.explanation: A public slip in front of everyone, repeated with emphasis, shows embarrassment.
quests.textToSpeak: I called the teacher 'Mom' in front of the whole class. Everyone heard it. Everyone.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Pay attention to what the speaker's body is doing.
quests.explanation: Eyes closing on their own after a long shift is a clear sign of tiredness.
quests.textToSpeak: I've been answering calls since seven this morning. My eyes are closing on their own, and my coffee's cold again.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker says about the other person's effort.
quests.explanation: Gratitude fits because the speaker is thanking someone for going out of their way.
quests.textToSpeak: You stayed after the shop closed just to help me find the right size? That's really kind of you.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice who the speaker is comparing themselves with.
quests.explanation: The speaker sees others connecting while they stand alone, which is different from just having nothing to do. Loneliness is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: Everybody at the party seems to have someone to talk to. I've been standing by the snacks for an hour.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Ask what the speaker is doing instead of listening.
quests.explanation: Doodling while a lecture goes on shows the speaker's attention has drifted. The speaker is bored.
quests.textToSpeak: Twenty minutes into this lecture, and I've already forgotten what he said. I'm just drawing circles on my page.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what is going to happen tonight.
quests.explanation: A big first step is only hours away, and the speaker's energy shows it. Excitement is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: I got the keys this morning. Tonight I'm sleeping in my very own apartment!

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to how the speaker explains why a 'small' prize matters.
quests.explanation: A year of daily effort makes the small trophy meaningful. That's pride.
quests.textToSpeak: Look, I know it's just a small trophy, but I trained every morning for a year to get it.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about what the noise is getting in the way of.
quests.explanation: The music interferes with the speaker's sleep, an everyday irritation. The speaker is annoyed.
quests.textToSpeak: The neighbors are playing loud music again, and it's eleven at night. I have to be up at six.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the difference between what Mom says and what the speaker believes.
quests.explanation: The speaker doubts the reassurance and fears the cough is serious. That's worry about a family member.
quests.textToSpeak: Mom's been coughing all week, and she keeps saying it's nothing. I don't think it's nothing.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice how the speaker reacts when Grandma won't explain.
quests.explanation: The unanswered story makes the speaker want to know more. This is curiosity.
quests.textToSpeak: Grandma keeps talking about a red door in her old town, but when I ask, she just smiles. What was behind it?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about what the handwriting stands for.
quests.explanation: The handwriting keeps the person present while the speaker sorts through what's left. So sad is the best fit.
quests.textToSpeak: I'm packing my grandfather's books into boxes. His handwriting is still in the margins.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about how the speaker would feel after realizing the mistake.
quests.explanation: A small public misunderstanding makes the speaker feel awkward. Everything points to embarrassment.
quests.textToSpeak: I waved back at a stranger because I thought he was waving at me. He was calling a taxi.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice which achievement the speaker chooses to point out.
quests.explanation: The speaker highlights the daughter's achievement with admiration. That's pride.
quests.textToSpeak: My daughter gave her first speech tonight, and she never looked down at her notes. Not once.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Pay attention to what the speaker's body is doing now that the danger is over.
quests.explanation: The racing heart calming after making the train shows the tension is over. Relief is the natural reading.
quests.textToSpeak: The train was late, but I made it. I sat down, and honestly, my heart is only now slowing down.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Think about what that place used to mean to the speaker.
quests.explanation: The speaker links a place that's gone with time spent with Dad. Remembering something lost brings sadness.
quests.textToSpeak: We walked past the old movie theater today. It's a parking lot now. Dad used to take me there every Saturday.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice how the small problems pile up one after another.
quests.explanation: A chain of minor inconveniences is irritating without being a disaster. Annoyance is the feeling here.
quests.textToSpeak: The flight was delayed two hours, then the gate changed, and now the only seat left is next to the toilets.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice who the speaker has talked to since arriving.
quests.explanation: Having only brief contact with a cashier suggests the speaker has no real connection yet. This is loneliness.
quests.textToSpeak: It's my first month in this city. I've talked to the cashier at the corner shop, and that's about it.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the question at the end, and whether the speaker blames anyone.
quests.explanation: The speaker has conflicting instructions and simply can't tell what to do. That's confusion, not hostility.
quests.textToSpeak: They told me to give it to Dana, then Dana said Mark, and now none of it makes sense. Who do I actually give it to?

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice what information is missing from the boss's request.
quests.explanation: An unexplained summons with a serious instruction makes the speaker fear what's coming.
quests.textToSpeak: The boss just asked to see me in her office. She didn't say why. She only said, 'Close the door.'

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to the two pieces of news and decide how they affect the speaker.
quests.explanation: Both messages are good for the speaker, so the reaction is pleasure. This is happiness.
quests.textToSpeak: The landlord called. He's not raising the rent this year, and he's fixing the heater, too.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice how the speaker jokes about the bucket and what the joke is really about.
quests.explanation: The sarcasm about the 'permanent furniture' shows the speaker is fed up with the broken promise. This is anger.
quests.textToSpeak: He said Monday. It's Friday. The bucket under my sink is now permanent furniture.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Listen to what the speaker says about themselves before today's run.
quests.explanation: Pride fits because the speaker beat their own expectations.
quests.textToSpeak: I did it. I ran the whole three miles without stopping, and I was never a runner.

quests.instruction: How are they feeling? Lock in the right emotion.
quests.hint: Notice the fact the speaker uses to show it was unexpected.
quests.explanation: The relatives are somewhere the speaker didn't expect them to be. This is surprise.
quests.textToSpeak: Wait, you're all here? You live in three different cities!
